title: Unmanned Aircraft Systems Operations Technician
raw_text:
8-150. MOS 150U--Unmanned Aircraft Systems Operations Technician
  a. Licensing/certification requirements. None.
  b. Prerequisite. DA Cir 601 series.
  c. MOS 150U. MOS 150U is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is 15W and 15E.
15W candidates must be qualified as a Vehicle Air Operator (AO)/Mission Payload Operator (PO)
in one of the following UAS: Hunter, Shadow, or ERMP. Warrant officer application packet will be
reviewed by Aviation Personnel Proponency. Must be selected by the Warrant Officer Panel.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) B--Aviation Safety Officer.
         (4) P--Parachutist.
         (5) T--Transition.
         (6) Z--Research, Development, Test and Evaluation.
  d. Associated ASI. (Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant
officer MOS)).
         (1) 5A--Joint Air Tactical Operations Officer.
         (2) 5U--Air Operations Officer.
         (3) C8--Air Defense Airspace Management (ADAM) / Brigade Aviation Element (BAE)
(Effective 201710).
         (4) G3—Air Cavalry Leaders Course.
         (5) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (Effective 202410).
  e. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial awarding of MOS 150U.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Successfully complete the Aviation Warrant Officer Basic Course.
              (b) Meet vision and hearing standards of AR 40-501 for assignment of warrant officer.
to Aviation Branch, normal color discrimination per AR 40-501 and have full use of both hands.
              (c) A physical demand Rating of Moderate (GOLD).
              (d) Qualifying Scores. A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ)-0120cm, Seated
Power Throw (PT)-0350cm, Strength Deadlift (SD)-0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR)-0036
shuttles in Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
              (e) Must be a U.S. citizen and possess at least an interim SECRET eligibility prior to
warrant officer candidate school.
              (f) Successfully complete the TUAS operations technician training for award of MOS
150U.
         (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (1).
              (b) Successfully complete the Aviation Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
         (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (2).
              (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course.
         (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (3).
              (b) Must successfully complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course.
  f. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
              (a) Supervise TUAS operations, to include mission planning, mission payload
operation, launching, remotely piloting, and recovering.
              (b) Maintains a detailed knowledge of airspace requirements to plan flight missions
within acceptable mission profiles.
              (c) Coordinates with higher and subordinate units for employment of TUAS missions.
              (d) Develops and implements a TUAS standardization and safety program per all
applicable regulations.
              (e) Establishes and maintains a unit level Aircrew Training Program (ATP).
              (f) Supervises employment of TUASs to conduct air reconnaissance/target detection
or target engagement.
         (2) CW3--
             (a) Performs all duties outlined in paragraph g(1).
            (b) Develops and instructs newly appointed warrant officers during their entry level
training.
        (3) CW4--Performs all duties outlined in paragraph g (2).
        (4) CW5--Performs all duties outlined in paragraph g (3).
  g. Grading and position titles. Authorized position titles are provided in tables 6-2 and 6-3. The
following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals
WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the
following standards of grade table:
        (1) Table 8-150U-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
        (2) Table 8-150U-2. Standards of grade TDA.
  h. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to
each skill level are listed in the following table:
         (1) Table 8-150U-3. Physical requirements.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
